newsitem.title: CHILE: Cyprus Amax begins El Abra exploration.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Amax begins El Abra exploration.

text.p: U.S. mining company Cyprus Amax Minerals will invest $3 million this year in exploring for reserves at its recently built El Abra copper mine in northern Chile, head of exploration David Watkins, said.
"We are actively exploring around El Abra and have indications that we may be able to increase reserves at the deposit," Watkins told a news conference.
The prospecting, which began this year, is still in a very preliminary stage, he added.
Cyprus owns 51 percent of 225,000-tonne El Abra which started producing copper cathodes last year.
The rest is held by Chile's state copper company Codelco.
The mine, the world's largest heap-leaching operation, has proven oxide reserves of 800 million tonnes which sit above a large sulphide deposit.
Cyprus has started studies on ways to exploit the sulphide reserves, said the mine's general manager Johan von Loebenstein.
"We have started preliminary studies on the sulphides but we have not done any drilling," he said.
The mine has known sulphide reserves of nearly 600 million tonnes with a relatively low 0.6 percent copper grade.
The exploration budget at El Abra is in addition to the $3.5-4 million Cyprus is planning to invest looking for copper and gold in the mineral-rich arid north, said Watkins.
A large part of the program involves exploration for gold in the Maricunga gold belt where the company owns 50 percent of the Refugio gold mine, he said.
"We started to accelerate our program in the Maricunga in the last one and a half years when Refugio started to look viable," he said.
Refugio, owned equally with Canada's Bema Gold, came into production last year.
